name: I love you hand sign
blurb: Thumb, index and pinky up: the ASL I love you sign, not the rock horns
aka: I love you in sign language
rock on vs I love you
title: I Love You Hand Sign (ILY): ASL Meaning vs Rock On Horns
description: I love you hand sign reference: the ASL ILY gesture with thumb, index and pinky raised, how it differs from rock on horns, and how to draw and pose it.
answer: The I love you hand sign comes from American Sign Language: the thumb, index finger and little finger are raised while the middle and ring fingers fold down. It merges the ASL letters I, L and Y into one handshape. If the thumb is tucked in instead, the gesture becomes the rock on horns, which means something else.

sections.h: Where the ILY sign comes from
body: In American Sign Language the little finger alone spells I, thumb and index make L, and thumb plus little finger make Y. Raise all three at once and you have I-L-Y, I love you. Deaf communities have used the handshape for a long time, and it later spread into everyday hearing culture as a friendly goodbye, a cheer and a photo pose.
In character art it reads as warm and sincere, a step more personal than a wave or a peace sign.

sections.h: ILY sign vs rock on vs shaka

head: Gesture
Fingers up
Meaning
rows: Index and little finger; thumb holds the folded fingers

body: The thumb is the whole difference between love and rock. In some Mediterranean and Latin American countries the horns can also be an insult, so the distinction matters.

sections.h: How to draw the ILY hand

ul: Show the palm to the viewer; the ASL sign is normally made palm forward.
The thumb sticks out to the side at roughly a right angle, clearly separate from the index finger.
Middle and ring fingers fold to the palm together; draw their knuckles as a small bump, not two flat lines.
The little finger is noticeably shorter than the index. Making them equal is the most common error.
Keep the wrist straight; a bent wrist makes it look like a claw.

body: Hold the hand at shoulder or cheek height, palm toward the lens, and check in the preview that the thumb is visible; from some angles it hides behind the index finger and the pose turns into horns.
A gentle smile suits the meaning better than a shout. For a two-person shot, both people making the sign toward each other reads clearly as affection.

faq.q: What is the difference between I love you and rock on hand signs?
faq.a: I love you has the thumb out along with the index and little fingers. Rock on horns keep the thumb folded over the middle fingers.

faq.q: Which hand do you use for I love you in sign language?
faq.a: Either; signers use their dominant hand, palm facing the person they are signing to.

faq.q: Is the ILY sign the same as the shaka?
faq.a: No. The shaka raises only the thumb and little finger and means hang loose; the ILY sign adds the index finger.
